description: A graduate course on designing, evaluating and evolving large software systems around their quality attributes. Students model architectures in the diagram studio, run them on the cloud console, write code to enforce structural rules and defend decisions in review sessions.
modelledOn: Bass, Clements and Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice
Richards and Ford, Fundamentals of Software Architecture
outcomes: Specify quality attribute requirements as testable scenarios and select tactics that achieve them.
Evaluate an architecture with structured trade-off analysis and report risks, sensitivity points and trade-off points.
Design service-based and event-driven systems with explicit consistency, resilience and observability decisions.
Structure systems for modularity and evolution using fitness functions and migration strategies.
Document architecture with views and decision records, and measure and prioritise architectural technical debt.

units.title: Quality attributes and tactics
topics: Quality attribute scenarios: source, stimulus, environment, artefact, response and measure
Availability tactics: redundancy, heartbeat, failover and circuit breaker
Performance tactics: caching, concurrency, resource arbitration and load shedding
Security tactics: authentication, authorisation, least privilege, audit and zero trust boundaries
Modifiability and testability tactics: encapsulation, indirection, seams and dependency injection
Utility trees and prioritising conflicting requirements

units.title: Architecture evaluation and trade-off analysis
topics: ATAM: scenarios, approaches, sensitivity points, trade-off points and risks
Cost-benefit analysis of architectural strategies
Quantifying qualities: latency budgets, availability arithmetic and capacity models
Prototyping and load testing to validate an architectural decision
Lightweight architecture reviews and checklists
Conformance checking: dependency rules and architecture tests

units.title: Microservices and event-driven styles
topics: Service decomposition with domain-driven design: bounded contexts and aggregates
Synchronous and asynchronous communication: REST, gRPC and message brokers
Event-driven architecture: publish-subscribe, event sourcing and CQRS
Distributed data consistency: sagas, the outbox pattern and idempotency
Resilience patterns: timeouts, retries with backoff, bulkheads and rate limiting
API gateways, service discovery and observability: logs, metrics and traces
When not to use microservices: the modular monolith

units.title: Architecture of data-intensive and ML systems
topics: Batch, stream, lambda and kappa architectures
Data platforms: warehouse, lake and lakehouse; pipeline orchestration
ML system anatomy: training pipeline, feature store, model registry and serving
Monitoring ML systems: data drift, feedback loops and hidden technical debt
Architectures for low-connectivity settings: offline-first mobile money and health apps

units.title: Modularity and evolvability
topics: Coupling, cohesion, information hiding and connascence
Layered, hexagonal and clean architecture
Dependency inversion and plug-in architectures
Evolutionary architecture and fitness functions
API versioning, backward compatibility and schema evolution
Migration strategies: the strangler fig pattern and branch by abstraction

units.title: Architecture documentation and decision records
topics: Views and viewpoints: the C4 model, module, component-connector and allocation views
Architecture decision records: context, decision, consequences and status
Architecture description standards and stakeholder concerns
Diagrams as code and keeping documentation in the repository
Communicating architecture to executives, developers and operators

units.title: Architectural technical debt
topics: The technical debt metaphor: principal, interest, deliberate and inadvertent debt
Finding debt: dependency cycles, hotspots, change coupling and code churn
Structural metrics: instability, abstractness, distance from the main sequence and design structure matrices
Quantifying interest and prioritising repayment
Architectural refactoring: breaking cycles, extracting modules and splitting databases
Governance: debt registers, quality gates and architecture review boards

units.title: Capstone: architecture in practice
topics: Architecture kata: design a system from a short business brief under time pressure
Defending trade-offs to a review panel
Peer architecture review with written findings
Emerging concerns: AI-assisted development, sustainability and sovereignty

schedule.title: Quality attribute scenarios and early tactics
schedule.exercise: Write six quality attribute scenarios for a mobile money transfer service, then pick one availability tactic and one performance tactic for each and state its cost.

tasks.title: Rewrite five vague requirements such as 'must be fast' as six-part scenarios with measurable response measures and record them in a table
Add a circuit breaker with timeout and fallback around a flaky service call in code, and test its open and half-open states
Add a cache and a load-shedding rule to an overloaded service, and compare 99th percentile latency before and after under a load spike

schedule.title: Security, modifiability and conflicting qualities
schedule.exercise: Build a utility tree for an online health-records system, rate each scenario by importance and difficulty, and identify two pairs of attributes that conflict.

tasks.title: Mark trust boundaries and the authentication and audit tactics on an architecture diagram for a payment gateway
Introduce a seam and dependency injection to make a hard-wired payment module testable, and write a test with a fake provider
Rank competing quality attribute scenarios for a rural clinic system with limited budget, justify the priorities, and record the stakeholder reaction

schedule.title: Structured architecture evaluation
schedule.exercise: Run a mini ATAM on a ride-hailing backend: list scenarios, approaches, sensitivity points, trade-off points and risks, then compare two strategies with cost-benefit scores.

tasks.title: Classify findings from a sample evaluation into risks, sensitivity points and trade-off points and map each to a scenario
Score three architectural strategies on benefit, cost and uncertainty, compute their return ratios, and rank them
Compute end-to-end availability and latency budget for a chain of five services and find which one violates the stated scenario

schedule.title: Validating decisions and conformance
schedule.exercise: Design a load test that validates the throughput claim behind a messaging decision, and write three dependency rules that an automated architecture test should enforce.

tasks.title: Walk a one-page checklist review of a sample design and record the five issues you would raise with evidence
Load test two designs, one with a queue and one without, increase request rate, and report the saturation point of each
Write an architecture test that fails the build when a domain package imports an infrastructure package, and show it catching a violation

schedule.title: Decomposition, communication and events
schedule.exercise: Decompose an online marketplace into bounded contexts, choose synchronous or asynchronous calls for each interaction, and show where event sourcing would help audit.

tasks.title: Draw bounded contexts and a context map for an e-commerce domain, naming the aggregates and relationships between contexts
Implement the same order flow as a synchronous call chain and with a message queue, and compare failure behaviour when one service is down
Build an event-sourced account that rebuilds balance from events, add a CQRS read model, and show eventual consistency under load

schedule.title: Consistency, resilience and observability
schedule.exercise: Design a saga for booking a bus seat with payment and notification steps, list the compensation for each, and explain when a modular monolith is the better choice for a team of five.

tasks.title: Add timeouts and retries with exponential backoff to a client and show how unbounded retries create a retry storm
Implement a saga with compensation for a three-step booking, inject a failure at step three, and verify the system returns to consistent state
Deploy the same application as three services and as a modular monolith, compare latency, cost and operational steps, and recommend one

schedule.title: Data-intensive and ML system architecture
schedule.exercise: Sketch the architecture of a crop-disease detection service from phone photos, covering training, serving, drift monitoring and offline operation for farmers with poor coverage.

tasks.title: Draw an ML system showing data ingestion, feature store, training, registry and serving, and label where each can fail
Compute a rolling count from a stream of events in batch and in streaming style and compare latency and correctness for late events
Detect data drift in a feature stream with a statistical test, raise an alert, and describe the retraining trigger and the rollback plan

schedule.title: Coupling, layering and plug-ins
schedule.exercise: Take a layered application with a database call inside a controller, refactor it to a hexagonal structure with ports and adapters, and justify each dependency direction.

tasks.title: Identify three kinds of coupling in a given code sample and reduce one of them by introducing an interface
Redraw a layered system as ports and adapters and show how the domain is isolated from the database and the web framework
Build a plug-in architecture for payment providers, add a third provider without changing core code, and prove it with tests

schedule.title: Evolving systems safely
schedule.exercise: Plan a staged migration of a legacy billing monolith to services using the strangler fig pattern, with fitness functions that guard performance and coupling at each stage.

tasks.title: Evolve a JSON API by adding an optional field and show an old client still works, then break compatibility deliberately
Write two fitness functions, one for response time and one for dependency direction, and run them in a build pipeline
Route 10, 50 then 100 percent of traffic from a legacy service to a replacement, and roll back when an error rate threshold is crossed

schedule.title: Documenting architecture and decisions
schedule.exercise: Document one system at the context, container and component levels of the C4 model, and write three decision records including one you would now reverse.

tasks.title: Produce context and container diagrams for a school management system and check each element has a name, technology and purpose
Write a decision record for choosing a message broker, listing options considered, drivers, decision, and consequences accepted
Present the same architecture to a finance director, a developer and an operations lead, and adapt the content to each concern

schedule.title: Detecting and measuring architectural debt
schedule.exercise: Given a dependency graph and commit history, find cycles and change-coupled files, compute instability and abstractness for each module, and list the three worst offenders.

tasks.title: Classify ten described shortcuts as deliberate or inadvertent and prudent or reckless debt, and say which would you accept
Detect dependency cycles in a module graph with code and list the smallest set of edges whose removal breaks them all
Compute instability and abstractness for twelve modules, plot distance from the main sequence, and flag modules in the zone of pain

schedule.title: Paying down debt and governing it
schedule.exercise: Estimate the interest paid per sprint on three debt items from lost developer hours, rank them by return on repayment, and propose a debt register and quality gate.

tasks.title: Draft a debt register for a system with six items, giving each an owner, impact, cost to fix and review date
Compute interest and payback for five debt items from lost developer hours and rank them for a two-sprint repayment budget
Break a cycle between two modules by extracting an interface, then re-run the dependency analysis to show the cycle is gone

schedule.title: Architecture kata, review and reflection
schedule.exercise: Design an architecture for a national vaccination tracking service from a one-page brief, present its main trade-offs, and write a review of a peer's design.

tasks.title: Produce a context diagram and three key decisions for a short business brief within a fixed time box
Review a peer's architecture, list strengths, risks and questions with scenario references, and rate the findings by severity
Deploy the core of your kata design, test one stated quality scenario with load or failure, and report whether the design meets it
